description: pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs line 118: ValidityMaxLint uses not_after.saturating_sub(not_before) to compute duration. The comment says "saturate to avoid underflow on malformed certs." If notAfter < notBefore, the saturating_sub produces 0, and 0 <= cap is always true, so the lint returns Pass for a cert with an inverted validity period. This is arguably correct (the cert is malformed but the lint does not flag it — another lint or pkix-path validity check should catch it). However, there is no test covering this edge case to document the intended behavior. A test with notAfter < notBefore should assert Pass (or document why) to make the behavior explicit.
title: P3: ValidityMaxLint test missing: no test for notAfter < notBefore (saturating_sub underflow path)
